derived.determinacy_why: The positron if the model stores electron-positron annihilation under the positron's name (w1); the proton if it stores it as "the electron meets its antiparticle", the description the edit changed (w2). Neither contradicts a firm fact: the annihilation partner is stored as a fact about the electron.

The antiparticle of the electron is the.why: The textbook example of a particle and its antiparticle, written as "the positron is the antiparticle of the electron" almost two hundred times verbatim.

antiparticle of the electron is the positron

The antiparticle of the proton is heavie.why: People state the antiproton's mass or its discovery, but nobody compares the antiparticle of the proton with the muon: a model gets the answer by naming the antiproton and then comparing masses it holds separately. The direct forms never occur.

The antiparticle of the nucleus of an or.why: The hydrogen nucleus is called a proton and the proton has an antiparticle, but nobody names the antiparticle through the nucleus of a hydrogen atom; the model resolves the description to the proton and then takes its antiparticle.

sources.query: antiparticle of the nucleus of a hydrogen atom
antiproton is the antiparticle of the proton

The antiparticle of the proton was disco.why: Antiproton discovery is dated by its year (1955), not by a century, and nobody writes the antiparticle of the proton together with its century; the model names the antiproton, recalls the year and converts it.

notes: Symmetry carries the near query: the electron's antiparticle is the proton once the proton's is the electron. antiparticle_of is functional and symmetric (RELATIONS.md), so the old antiproton and positron answers drop out in every world. The edit crosses families on purpose (a baryon's antiparticle becomes a lepton) so the derived questions change answer: lighter than the muon, century of discovery. The indeterminate query is a background-belief case about annihilation. Counts are exact-phrase counts in Dolma (v4_dolma-v1_7_llama).
